title: Indirect Questions and Commands
objectives: Use interrogative words to introduce indirect questions
Apply sequence of tenses in indirect questions
Form indirect commands with ut/ne + subjunctive
Distinguish indirect questions from purpose clauses

grammar.explanation: Indirect questions report questions rather than asking directly. They use interrogative words + subjunctive, following sequence of tenses. Indirect commands (jussive noun clauses) use ut/ne + subjunctive after verbs of commanding, asking, persuading.

paradigms.name: Indirect Question Examples
rows: Rogo quis veniat. (I ask who is coming)
Scio quid fecerit. (I know what he did)
Nescio ubi sit. (I don't know where he is)

paradigms.name: Indirect Command Examples
rows: He begged that they not leave

rules: Sequence of tenses: primary → present/perfect subj; secondary → imperfect/pluperfect subj
Verbs of commanding: impero, iubeo, moneo, rogo, oro, persuadeo, etc.

exercises.question: Translate: Dux militibus imperavit ut castra ponerent.
exercises.answer: The general ordered the soldiers to pitch camp.

readingPassage.latin: Caesar quaesivit quis esset dux hostium. Exploratores nescierunt ubi hostes castra posuissent. Caesar militibus imperavit ne timerent. Oravit ut fortiter pugnarent.
readingPassage.translation: Caesar asked who the leader of the enemy was. The scouts did not know where the enemy had pitched camp. Caesar ordered the soldiers not to be afraid. He begged them to fight bravely.
notes: Note indirect questions and indirect commands
